A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the problem of matching users in mobility datasets, which is a fundamental building block in many applications, is a challenging one, and requires a careful analysis and design of the matching algorithm.
, in the case of two datasets with a large overlap of users, the matching process is feasible, and it can be expected that the matchability increases over time, as more data is collected.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the matchability of individuals in mobility datasets can be accurately predicted, and the expected success rates can be estimated in advance, given the statistical properties of the datasets and their frequency of data collection.
, in the context of matching users across datasets, we can expect to be able to match individuals based on their mobility traces in large datasets.

, despite the large number of users and the large number of records, it is possible to identify a subset of users that will be highly likely to be matched in a short time interval, and this subset will increase with the frequency of the data collection.
